Supplementary information 
 
 
Supplementary Material and Methods 
 
Relative quantification of gene expression by real-time PCR 
To confirm the array-based gene expression findings, six genes that were 
differentially expressed in LGFMS tumors were selected for real-time PCR. TaqMan gene 
expression assays (Applied Biosystems, Foster City, CA, USA) were used for the relative 
quantification of CASR (Assay ID: Hs01047794_m1), CD24 (Hs02379687_s1), FOXL1 
(Hs01124449_s1) and TMPRSS2 (Hs01122327_m1) (upregulated in LGFMS), and SLC41A2 
(Hs00259767_m1) and TANC2 (Hs01562201_m1) (downregulated in LGFMS). When 
possible, assays were chosen that span exon-exon boundaries and are located to the 5´-end of 
the transcript. We also analyzed the expression of wt CREB3L2 (Hs01592193_m1), where the 
assay recognizes the exon 2 – exon 3 boundary of the transcript. The expression of four 
housekeeping genes (18S, ACTB, ABL1 and HPRT1) was evaluated in a subset of the tumor 
samples and the gene with the most stable expression across the samples, in this case 18S, was 
used as endogenous control to normalize for differences in sample cDNA input in subsequent 
analyses. LGFMS cases 1-8 and 12-14 were used for the real-time PCR analyses. The other 
cases could not be included due to lack of material. MFS, DFM, SFT and EMCS cases were 
used for comparison. The same RNA samples were analyzed with gene expression array and 
real-time PCR, except for two EMCS samples that were only analyzed with real-time PCR. 
The cDNA synthesis, using 1 ug of total RNA, and PCR reactions were performed as 
previously described (1). Each sample was analyzed in triplicate for each gene. The data were 
analyzed according to the comparative C
T method, where the relative input amounts of sample 
RNA is given by 2-CT (2). 
 
Detection of FUS-CREB3L2 protein in transfected HEK293 cells 
For the western blot, total protein lysates were prepared from control and transfected 
HEK293 cells using the Laemmli Sample buffer (Bio-Rad Laboratories, Hercules, CA, USA) 
according to the manufacturer’s instructions. The protein content from approximately 100,000 
cells was electrophoresed and western blotted as described (3). The murine anti-FLAG M2 
antibody (Stratagene) and the ECL anti-mouse HRP-linked secondary antibody (GE 
Healthcare, Waukesha, WI, USA) were used to detect the tagged proteins. The membranes

were visualized using the Amersham ECL Plus Western Blotting Detection Reagents (GE 
Healtcare) and the luminescent image analyzer LAS-4000 (Fujifilm Life Science, 
Woodbridge, CT, USA) according to the manufacturers’ instructions.  
For the ICC, control and FC-HEK cells were grown in 35 mm2 Petri dishes and then 
fixed by incubation with PBS containing 4 % paraformaldehyde and sucrose (pH 7.4) for 15 
minutes at room temperature. The fixed cells were washed twice with PBS for five minutes 
each and permeabilized by incubation with 0.25 % TRITONTM X-100 (Sigma-Aldrich, St. 
Louis, MO, USA) in PBS for 5 minutes, and then washed twice for five minutes with PBS. 
The cells were blocked by incubation with 10 % BSA in PBS for 30 minutes at 37C, and 
then incubated with the anti-FLAG M2 antibody at a 1/1000 dilution in 3 % BSA/PBS, for 
two hours at 37C. The cells were washed three times with PBS for five minutes and then 
incubated with an anti-mouse IgG FITC conjugated secondary antibody (Sigma-Aldrich) at a 
1/1000 dilution in 3 % BSA/PBS, for 45 minutes at 37C. Finally, the cells were washed three 
times for five minutes with PBS. Cells were counterstained with DAPI (for the detection of 
nuclei) and examined under the microscope as described (4). 
 
Construction of reporter gene plasmids 
The regulatory sequences of CD24 and FOXL1 were PCR amplified, restriction 
enzyme digested, subcloned between the NheI and XhoI sites of the vector pFLhRL upstream 
of the firefly luciferase gene and sequence verified according to standard procedures (5). 
pFLhRL, which contains both the firefly and Renilla luciferases, has been described before 
(5). The fragments were PCR amplified using the GeneAmp XL PCR kit, the three step 
cycling profile, and 300 ng DNA from the BAC clones RP11-973P11 (6q21, NCBI Build 37) 
or CTD-2336F9 (16q24, NCBI Build 37) (Invitrogen), respectively, according to the 
manufacturer’s instructions (Applied Biosystems). For the CD24 upstream region, the primers 
Chr6_1206FNheI (5´ GCCTGATCTCTGCTAGCTG) (forward) and Chr6_2237RXhoI (5´ 
CGGTCCCACTCGAGTTCAC) (reverse) (restriction enzyme sites in bold) were used, 
yielding a 1 kbp fragment. For the CD24 intronic region, the primers 726FNheI (5´ 
CCAGGTGGCTAGCTCCCACTTTC) (forward) and 1552RXhoI (5´ 
GGAGGAAGACACTCGAGTACGGT) (reverse) were used, yielding a 0.8 kbp fragment. 
The CD24 gene maps to 6q21, but several pseudogenes exist on other chromosomes (6). Due 
to the similarity between the CD24 pseudogene in Yq11 and the CD24 gene in 6q21, the 
genomic mapping of clone RP11-973P11 was confirmed with metaphase FISH on cells from

a healthy male individual using Cy3 labeled RP11-973P11 BAC DNA together with whole 
chromosome 6 painting (WCP) probes (Applied spectral imaging, Vista, CA, USA). BAC 
DNA labeling and hybridization was performed as described (4) (data not shown). Attempts 
were made to clone the entire putative promoter region of CD24 (-2080 to +200), however we 
were unable to amplify this sequence from RP11-973P11 DNA or total DNA from a healthy 
female individual. For the FOXL1 promoter region, the primers FOXL11629FNheI (5´ 
ATTTCTACAGCTAGCTGCCATC) (forward) and FOXL1pInRXhoI (5´ 
GAAGCTCTCGAGACTTGTCGGAG) (reverse) were used, yielding a 2.4 kbp fragment. 
 
Combined CD24 ICC and FISH 
 Cell cultures from Cases 5 and 6 were washed  in PBS, fixed in cold methanol for 
five to ten minutes and air-dryed, and then rehydrated for 30 minutes in 1 % BSA/PBS. The 
slides were incubated 60 minutes at room temperature with a murine anti-human CD24 FITC 
conjugated monoclonal antibody (SN3/ab30350, Abcam, Cambridge, UK) at 1:100 dilution. 
To enhance the fluorescence signal, the slides were incubated with an anti-mouse IgG FITC 
conjugated secondary antibody for 30 minutes. After incubation, the slides were washed twice 
for five minutes each in 1 % BSA/PBS and then dehydrated in ethanol. The cover slips were 
removed by five minutes immersion in absolute ethanol and rehydrated in PBS for five 
minutes. Bound antibodies were fixed by immersion in 1 % formaldehyde for five minutes 
and the slides were then washed for five minutes in PBS and dehydrated in ethanol. 
Interphase FISH was performed on the same slides by co-hybridization of BAC probes for the 
FUS (BAC RP11-388M20) and CREB3L2 (BACs RP11-29B3 and RP11-377B19) loci (NCBI 
Build 37, BACPAC Resource Center, Oakland, CA, USA). The BAC DNA was directly 
labeled with Cy3 (RP11-388M20) or biotin (RP11-29B3 and RP11-377B19) as described (4). 
The probes and slides were co-denatured for five to ten minutes at 85C and hybridization 
was performed in a humid chamber over night at 37C. Post-hybridization washes were 
performed as described (4) and analysis as described above.

Supplementary figure legends 
 
Figure S1. Real-time PCR of genes differentially expressed in LGFMS (blue). MFS (white), 
DFM (black), SFT (yellow) and EMCS (pink) samples were used for comparison. Bars 
represent median expression values together with the 25
th to 75th percentiles. The genes 
FOXL1, CD24, CASR, and TMPRSS2 were upregulated in LGFMS, while TANC2 and 
SLC41A2 were downregulated. CASR expression was not detected in MFS, DFM or EMCS 
and TMPRSS2 was not detected in DFM, SFT or EMCS (CT ≥ 35). Wt CREB3L2 was 
expressed in all tumor types. 
 
Figure S2. Combined FISH and ICC analysis of cells from LGFMS Cases 6 (A) and 5 (B). A 
and B, The FISH results showed that the cells had a CREB3L2 rearrangement (separated blue 
signals) and FUS-CREB3L2 fusion (colocalized blue and red signals). The same cells 
displayed cytoplasmic CD24 expression (green). Images of nuclei (DAPI stain) with FISH 
signals are inserted. C, The positive control, human prostate carcinoma cells, displayed the 
same pattern of CD24 expression. D, The negative control, HEK293 cells, lacked the 
cytoplasmic staining of CD24. 
 
Figure S3. Translocation breakpoint-associated deletions (A, B) and 7q gains (C) identified 
by SNP array analysis. Vertical broken lines show the approximate location of translocation 
breakpoints, horizontal lines the deletions. Black boxes and lines denote exons. Locations are 
according to the genome assembly UCSC hg18. A, Cases 2, 3, 5 and 6 had deletions telomeric 
to the CREB3L2 exon 5 breakpoints, Case 6 had an additional 7q33 deletion centromeric to 
CREB3L2, involving the DGKI gene. B, Deletions centromeric to the FUS breakpoints (Case 
2; exon 7, Case 5; intron 7 and Case 6; exon 6). Cases 2 and 6 also displayed 16p11 deletions 
telomeric to FUS involving the genes STX1B (Case 2) and BCKDK and MYST1 (Case 6). C, 
The complex pattern of 7q gains observed in Case 4, suggesting heterogeneous ring 
chromosomal content. A deletion of CREB3L2 in this case could not be determined. BAF: B 
allele frequency. 
 
Figure S4. Scatter plots of the expression values of genes involved in Hedgehog signaling 
(FOXL1, FOXF1, GLI1, SHH, PTCH1 and GLI2). FOXL1 was identified as the top 
upregulated gene in LGFMS (blue) compared to the other tumor groups; DFM (black), EMCS 
(pink), MFS (white) and SFT (yellow). Also FOXF1 was specifically upregulated in LGFMS.

GLI1, SHH, PTCH1 and GLI2 were upregulated in LGFMS, although not displaying clearly 
LGFMS-specific expression. The asterisk () marks the LGFMS outlier sample (Case 8) 
identified from global gene expression analysis.
